ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: {SUBJECT} about the place
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A colonist fond of animals has always loved one kind most, and it lives on this land (or is roaming the map). They'd like the colony to have one. With PokéWorld, a favourite Pokémon, caught in a ball.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.lostText: {OTHER_nameDef}, the animal {FOR_nameDef} always wanted, is no longer the colony's.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: The colony has {SUBJECT} of its own: tamed (or, for a Pokémon, caught). If it bonds to {FOR_nameDef}, that will mean more to {FOR_objective} still. Promised, a calm one out on the land is marked for taming.

plain.li: I've loved them since I was small. I'd give a lot to have {SUBJECT} about the place.
They live round here, you know. I've seen the tracks. Why shouldn't we have {SUBJECT} of our own?
Some people love horses, some love dogs. For me it's always been {SUBJECT}.
[child] Can we have {SUBJECT}? I'd look after it every single day.
[lowmood] Just having {SUBJECT} around would make this place feel more like home.
[spring] It's the time of year for young ones. If we were ever going to bring {SUBJECT} home, it's now.
[old] I've wanted {SUBJECT} my whole life. I'd like to have one about before I'm done.

warm.li: It would get the warmest corner I could find. I'd see to it every morning before I saw to myself.
I don't need it to be mine. I'd just like to see it every morning.

blunt.li: Bring home {SUBJECT}. I've asked for less, but never wanted anything more.

cheerful.li: Imagine {SUBJECT}, here, with us! I've already thought of a name.
I've drawn them on every scrap of paper I've ever had. Now I'd like a real one.

gloomy.li: Everyone has something they love. Mine lives out past the fields, and it doesn't know we're here.

cold.li: I'm fond of the kind, and it would earn its keep. Bringing {SUBJECT} home is time well spent.

plain.li: There it is. I keep going to look at it.
I've wanted one of these for as long as I can remember. Now we have one.

warm.li: I'll look after it. I promised myself I would, years ago.

cheerful.li: Come and see it! It's even better up close.

gloomy.li: I didn't think I'd ever really have one.

cold.li: Exactly what I wanted. Thank you.

plain.li: Maybe one day. They're still out there.

gloomy.li: Out past the fields, where they always are.

blunt.li: Then I'll keep drawing them. It's all I've got.

plain.li: I saw the tracks again this morning.

cheerful.li: Still thinking about {SUBJECT}. Still thinking of names.

ColonyCouncil.WishDef.label: a pack animal of {FOR_possessive} own
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.description: A hauler, someone with a trader's gift for talk, or a restless soul who'd rather be on the road wants a pack animal that is theirs: its master, or bonded to it. Only where the colony has one going spare or the land has pack animals it could tame.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.lostText: {FOR_nameDef}'s pack animal doesn't answer to {FOR_objective} any more.
ColonyCouncil.WishDef.fulfilledWhen: {FOR_nameDef} is master of a pack animal, or bonded to one. One like {SUBJECT} would do. Set its master in the Animals tab, or promise it: one of the colony's with no master is made {FOR_possessive}, else a calm one out on the land is marked for taming.

plain.li: I carry everything on my back, and {SUBJECT} could carry twice as much without complaining.
Every trip to the far fields I'm hauling back and forth. With {SUBJECT} of my own, it would be one trip.
[skill:Social] Someone who trades needs something to carry the goods. Give me {SUBJECT} and I'll do the talking.
[lowmood] I'd like something that walks beside me and carries the load. It doesn't have to be clever.
[winter] Hauling wood through the snow on my own back, again. Give me {SUBJECT} to share the load.

warm.li: I'd treat it well. It would earn its keep and get the best of the hay.

blunt.li: Give me a pack animal. I'm tired of being one.

cheerful.li: Me and {SUBJECT}, on the road together! Well, to the far field and back.

gloomy.li: My back's going. Something has to carry this stuff, and soon it won't be me.

cold.li: A pack animal triples what one person can move. Assign one to me.

plain.li: It follows me now, loaded up and patient. Good animal.

warm.li: We'll get on, the two of us.

cheerful.li: Look how much it can carry!

plain.li: I'll carry it myself. I always have.
